'''Feroze Gujral''' is an Indian philanthropist, patron of the arts, businesswoman, columnist, media personality and former 
[[Model (person)|model]].<ref name="gujralfoundation.org">{{Cite web|title=Gujral Foundation – The Gujral Foundation|url=https://gujralfoundation.org/|access-date=2020-08-07|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Early life and family==
Feroze was born in Hyderabad, India in 1965. Her mother Viqar is of half-[[Hyderabadis|Hyderabadi]] and half-British descent, while her father George Ewari is of half-Arab and half-[[Malayali people|Malayali]] descent.<ref>[https://www.ft.com/content/a2f0a180-ecc2-11e4-a81a-00144feab7de Venice Biennale: India-Pakistan art collaboration]. 1 May 2015. ''[[FT.com]]''</ref>

She did her schooling from [[The Lawrence School, Sanawar]] in [[Himachal Pradesh]].<ref>[https://www.livemint.com/Leisure/7Kr0u2x6AGFVZgA0hKzJMN/Where-the-hills-come-alive.html Where the hills come alive]. 16 July 2010. ''[[livemint.com]]''</ref>

She has two siblings: brother Hanut Ewari, a philatelist, and a sister Anisha.<ref>[https://www.thenationalnews.com/arts-culture/art/feroze-gujral-india-s-very-own-peggy-guggenheim-1.846960 Feroze Gujral: India's very own Peggy Guggenheim?]. 9 April 2019. ''[[The National (Abu Dhabi)|The National News]]''.</ref>

She is married to Mohit Gujral, the son of Indian artist [[Satish Gujral]] (the brother of former prime minister [[I. K. Gujral]]) and has two children with him; Armaan Gujral, a businessman and Alaiia Gujral, an artist.<ref>[https://www.alaiiagujral.com/about About]. ''alaiiagujral.com''</ref>

==Career==
Feroze Gujral was spotted by Vidyun Singh and Asha Kocchar of Media Makers. One of the first ads she did was for Digjam Suitings with [[Shekhar Kapur]]. She was a popular model during the 1990s.

=== The Gujral Foundation and Outset India ===
She is the founder and director of The Gujral Foundation, a non-profit trust set up in 2008, along with her husband Mohit Gujral ( the son of the renowned Indian modern artist [[Satish Gujral]] ).<ref name="gujralfoundation.org"/> She is also the founder and director of Outset India, the Indian chapter of the Outset Contemporary Art Fund,<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Founder|url=http://outsetindia.org/the-founder/|access-date=2020-08-07|website=Outset India|language=en-US}}</ref> which is the largest acquisition art fund in the world, present in 9 countries, established in 2011.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=The Founder|url=http://outsetindia.org/the-founder/|access-date=2020-08-10|website=Outset India|language=en-US}}</ref>

Over the last decade, the Gujral Foundation has supported 150+ artists and 50+ exhibitions in India and internationally.<ref name=":0" /> Key projects include My East is Your West - a collateral event at the 56th Venice Biennale, curated by Feroze, produced and presented by the Foundation.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2017-10-23|title=Biennale Arte 2015 2015 {{!}} Biennale Arte 2015 - Eventi Collaterali|url=https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2015/biennale-arte-2015-eventi-collaterali|access-date=2020-08-10|website=La Biennale di Venezia|language=en}}</ref> The foundation has also commissioned projects for Contour Biennale 8, the 11th Shanghai Biennale, the 8th Berlin Biennale, the London Design Biennale and Kochi-Muziris Biennale.<ref name="gujralfoundation.org"/> Most recently the first architectural pavilion titled ‘The Song of the Earth and the Sky’ was displayed in the gardens of Sunder Nursery, New Delhi.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2020-02-23|title=This surprising exhibit in Delhi shows that origami isn't limited to just paper|language=en-US|work=Architectural Digest India|url=https://www.architecturaldigest.in/content/this-surprising-exhibit-in-delhi-shows-that-origami-isnt-limited-to-just-paper|access-date=2020-08-07}}</ref> They have supported numerous projects by other organizations including ‘V. S. Gaitonde at The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum,<ref>{{Cite web|title=V. S. Gaitonde: Painting as Process, Painting as Life|url=https://www.guggenheim.org/exhibition/v-s-gaitonde-painting-as-process-painting-as-life-2|access-date=2020-08-07|website=The Guggenheim Museums and Foundation}}</ref> ‘Forgotten Masters: Indian Painting for the [[East India Company]]’<ref>{{Cite web|last1=H|last2=yl|title=Forgotten Masters: Indian Painting for the East India Company – Lecture at the Wallace Collection – Gujral Foundation|url=https://gujralfoundation.org/forgotten-masters-indian-painting-for-the-east-india-company-lecture-at-the-wallace-collection/|access-date=2020-08-08|language=en-US|archive-date=21 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200821021353/https://gujralfoundation.org/forgotten-masters-indian-painting-for-the-east-india-company-lecture-at-the-wallace-collection/|url-status=dead}}</ref> at The Wallace Collection in the UK,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/dalrymplewill/status/1201830894606176256|access-date=2020-08-08|website=Twitter|language=en}}</ref> Colomboscope – Sea Change in Sri Lanka etc.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PARTNERS|url=https://www.colomboscope.lk/partners|access-date=2020-08-08|website=Colomboscope|language=en}}</ref>

The Foundation has strong educational institutional partnerships with [[CEPT University]]<ref name=":1" /> and Shiv Nadar University,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last1=H|last2=yl|title=October School {{!}} Oct 2018 – Gujral Foundation|url=http://gujralfoundation.org/october-school/|access-date=2020-08-10|language=en-US}}</ref> [[National Institute of Fashion Technology]] (NIFT) as well as other cultural institutions including Goethe-Institut, The Foundation for Indian Contemporary Art,<ref>{{Cite web|title=3 sentences on the curatorial|url=https://www.facebook.com/events/561809383947454/|access-date=2020-08-10|website=facebook.com}}</ref> Pro-Helvetia,<ref name="soundreasons.in">{{Cite web|title=Sound Reasons {{!}} Festival {{!}} records {{!}} Productions {{!}} Sound Art {{!}} Installations {{!}} Performances {{!}}|url=http://soundreasons.in/festival-14/|access-date=2020-08-10|website=soundreasons.in}}</ref> Japan Foundation,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-05-11|title=Queen-Size with light designer Jonathan O'Hear|url=https://prohelvetia.in/en/queen-size/|access-date=2020-08-10|website=Pro Helvetia India|language=en-GB}}</ref> Danish Art Foundation<ref name="soundreasons.in"/> and The Institute français en Inde.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mutations: Indo-French Image Encounters {{!}} Alkazi Foundation|url=https://alkazifoundation.org/mutations-indo-french-image-encounters/|access-date=2020-08-10|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Patronage and philanthropy ===
Feroze Gujral is regarded as one of India's leading art patrons. She is currently on the Trustee Board of Kochi Muziris Biennale of which she is a Founding Patron.<ref name=":2" /> She was previously on the international board of the Guggenheim Museum in New York, the Serpentine Gallery in London, and the advisory board of IGNCA, New Delhi.

Feroze has also been a funding patron for several years of artist grants, awards and prizes including the Gujral Foundation Excellence Award at CEPT University,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gujral Foundation Initiates Student Awards for Excellence - News - CEPT|url=https://cept.ac.in/news/gujral-foundation-initiates-student-awards-for-excellence|access-date=2020-08-10|website=cept.ac.in}}</ref> annual prizes at National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT). They also sponsor an art and a soccer prize at Gordonstoun School, UK.

Apart from the arts, the Gujral's have had a long-standing history of patronage and a number of initiatives have been started by the family post-partition including a school, orphanage, home for destitute women and the Pushpa Gujral Science City, all in Jalandhar, Punjab. They are also founder supporters of the forum for street children in Hyderabad, which includes a home for destitute boys that was started in 1989 by Feroze's mother. They also support various other NGOs like Nanhi Chaun (girl child), Save the Children and White Ribbon (safe childbirth). Feroze has for many years also been part of the young parliamentarian's initiative for malnutrition.{{citation needed|date=April 2022}}

=== Business ===
Feroze Gujral, aside from being a model and media personality, is also a businesswoman. Gujral ran a design studio called Fizzaro dealing in fine bone china products and customized table accessories, exporting to multiple countries.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Maddox|first=Georgina|date=2019-02-15|title=The catalyst named Feroze Gujral|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/art/the-catalyst-named-feroze-gujral/article26280811.ece|access-date=2020-08-10|issn=0971-751X}}</ref> She was a founding partner of Broadcast India, the first live broadband streaming platform in India. She was previously the Director of Design Plus, an architecture and design company, founded by her architect and real estate developer husband Mohit Gujral, and is the Founder Director of the international art design consultancy FMG advisors.

=== Ambassador and advisor ===
Feroze was also an ambassador for World Wildlife Fund, with a particular interest in the welfare of the Indian elephant. She is a volunteer for Teach for India and the curator for TEDx Delhi.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Feroze Gujral|url=https://www.womenofindiasummit.com/feroze-gujral|access-date=2020-08-08|website=women-of-india-3|language=en}}</ref> She has also been brand ambassador and advisor to numerous leading international fashion brands including Burberry,<ref>{{Cite web|title=40 GOING ON 30 - Indian Express|url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/40-going-on-30/650787/|access-date=2020-08-10|website=archive.indianexpress.com}}</ref> Tod's etc.

=== Media ===
As a contemporary cultural commentator, she has contributed multiple articles to publications including [[The Indian Express]], Financial Chronicle, Deccan Chronicle, Seminar, Vogue, Elle and Condé Nast Traveller amongst others.<ref>{{Cite web|title=About – Gujral Foundation|url=https://gujralfoundation.org/about/|access-date=2020-08-10|language=en-US}}</ref> She<ref name="Biographia">{{Cite web|last=Biographia|date=2020-07-29|title=Feroze Gujral Wiki-Biography-Age-Height-Weight-Profile-Info.|url=https://www.biographia.co.in/feroze-gujral/|access-date=2020-08-10|website=Biographia|language=en-US|archive-date=9 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809084450/https://www.biographia.co.in/feroze-gujral/|url-status=usurped}}</ref> was also host of her own TV show ‘Tonight with Feroze’.<ref name="Biographia"/>
